data.name: Generate a report from CSV data
data.description:
Parse a CSV string (first row must be a header) and render it as a complete, styled HTML report using the specified template.
Documentation: https://reportforge-api.vercel.app/docs
Quick Start:
- POST JSON { "csv": "header1,header2\nrow1col1,row1col2", "template": "sales-summary" } to /api/csv-to-report
- Content-Type: application/json required
- Free tier: no API key required (5 reports/day, 100 KB input). Paid tiers require an API key.
Parameters Explained:
- csv (required, string): Raw CSV text. First row must be a header row. Must have at least one data row.
- template (required, string): One of the supported templates (sales-summary, expense-report, inventory-status, invoice, project-status, payroll-summary, meeting-minutes).
- title (optional, string): Custom report title.
- delimiter (optional, string): Field delimiter character. Default: ",". Example: ";" for semicolon-separated CSV.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 INVALIDINPUT: Missing csv, malformed CSV, or unknown template. Ensure CSV has a header row and at least one data row.
- 401 UNAUTHORIZED: Missing or invalid API key when on a paid tier.
- 413 INPUTTOOLARGE: Payload exceeds tier size limit.
- 429 RATELIMITED: Daily report limit exceeded.
Edge Cases:
- CSV must include a header row; otherwise columns cannot be inferred.
- Use delimiter when input uses a non-comma separator.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Same tier limits as other report endpoints (Free: 5/day & 100 KB; Starter: 100/day & 2 MB; Business: unlimited & 10 MB). Daily reset at midnight UTC.

data.name: Public CSV Download (Queued/Scheduled Report)
data.description:
Public unauthenticated CSV download URL for a report run. This endpoint is typically surfaced via the report_run_csv_url field returned in ReportRuns or Poll for Queued Report Result when CsvReportVisibility is public.
Documentation / reference mentions: referenced in Create Queued Report and Report Runs docs (example downloads). No dedicated page, example usage shown in Create Queued Report docs.
Quick Start:
- If a report run includes report_run_csv_url and it points to a public path, you may GET that URL directly (no API key required) to download the CSV.
- Example URL pattern: https://reports.adzerk.com/r/{reportGuid}/srr/{runId}/e/{networkId}?filename={filename}
Parameters Explained (query):
- filename (optional): When present, server will set Content-Disposition to provide a suggested filename for the CSV.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 404 Not Found: The public URL expired or was not created (report run expired or was not granted public visibility).
- 403 Forbidden: The URL is not public; ensure CsvReportVisibility was set to public when queuing the report.
Edge Cases:
- Public download links expire (report runs persist for 10 days; link expiry may be shorter, documentation/example links mention 7-day link expiry for some UI links).
- Using filename query param will set Content-Disposition header with the requested filename if supported.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- These URLs are unauthenticated and should be treated as public; do not expose sensitive data if making them public.

data.name: Protected Assets Report - Export To Csv (DownloadCSV)
data.description:
Exports protected-assets report results to CSV and returns the CSV download stream.
Documentation: https://docs.cgn.portal.checkpoint.com/reference/protectedassetsreportexporttocsvdownloadcsvpost_v2protectedassetsreportexporttocsvdownloadcsv
Overview:
This POST endpoint requests generation (or retrieval) of a protected-assets CSV report and returns the CSV file as a download/stream. The request accepts a searchRequest object (simple filter/search payload) and supports recipients (an array of email addresses) for emailing the report.
Quick Start:
- Set the collection base URL ({{baseUrl}}) to https://api.dome9.com.
- Use HTTP Basic authentication (username/password).
- Send a POST to /v2/ProtectedAssetsReport/exportToCsv/downloadCSV with a JSON body containing searchRequest and, optionally, recipients.
- Minimum: supply valid Basic auth credentials and a body with any required search criteria; to receive emailed CSV, include recipients.
Parameters Explained:
- searchRequest (object, required-ish depending on backend): search/filter object for protected assets. The docs list recipients inside it. Provide other search fields if your integration requires them.
  - recipients (array of string): list of email addresses to which the report will be sent. Example: ["user@example.com"].
Headers:
- Content-Type: application/json (default). The API also lists application/x-www-form-urlencoded as an accepted content type for form-style requests.
- Accept: application/json or application/octet-stream/text/csv depending on client expectation. The endpoint typically returns CSV content with Content-Type: text/csv.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request — usually the body is missing or invalid (e.g., malformed JSON, missing required searchRequest fields). Ensure Content-Type: application/json and a valid JSON body.
- 401 Unauthorized — Basic auth missing or incorrect. Provide valid username/password credentials.
- 403 Forbidden — authenticated user lacks permission to generate/report exports. Verify account permissions/roles.
- 500 Internal Server Error — server-side issue; retry after a brief wait and contact support if it persists.
Edge Cases:
- If recipients are provided, the server may queue the email and return the CSV stream or a download token — behavior can vary; check response headers such as Content-Disposition and other returned metadata.
- CSV result may be large; client should be prepared to stream the response instead of buffering entirely in memory.
- Some clients / SDK examples may return a download token/UUID instead of direct CSV body. If you receive a token, call the appropriate download endpoint (site has related endpoints such as EntityReport/Download/{reportRequestUuid}).
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- The documentation page does not list explicit rate limits. Treat exports as potentially expensive operations — avoid frequent repeated exports in short bursts.

data.name: Protected Assets Report - Export To Csv
data.description:
Exports protected assets search results to CSV (generates an export job or sends CSV by email).
Documentation: https://docs.cgn.portal.checkpoint.com/reference/protectedassetsreportexporttocsvpost_v2protectedassetsreportexporttocsv
Quick Start:
- Set {{baseUrl}} to https://api.dome9.com
- Use Basic authentication (username/password)
- POST a JSON body containing the searchRequest object. To email the CSV include recipients in searchRequest.recipients.
Parameters Explained:
- searchRequest (object, required): Search request payload for selecting protected assets to export. At minimum you can provide:
  - recipients (array[string], optional): recipient email addresses to send the CSV by email. Example: ["{{recipientEmail}}"]
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Malformed JSON, missing required search criteria, or invalid parameter values. Ensure Content-Type: application/json and valid JSON body.
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or missing Basic credentials. Provide valid username/password.
- 403 Forbidden: Authenticated account lacks permission to run exports. Use an account with proper privileges.
- 500 Internal Server Error: Server-side failure — retry after a short wait and contact support if persistent.
Edge Cases:
- If recipients is empty or omitted, the API may queue the CSV for download rather than email it (behavior may vary by deployment).
- Very large result sets may queue background jobs — export may be asynchronous.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Not specified on this page. Respect organizational API rate limits and implement exponential backoff for retries.
data.evaluateGuide:

data.name: Protected Assets Report - Export To Csv (Download Link)
data.description:
Requests a download link for a previously prepared or newly generated Protected Assets Report CSV.
Documentation: https://docs.cgn.portal.checkpoint.com/reference/protectedassetsreportexporttocsvdownloadlinkpost_v2protectedassetsreportexporttocsvdownloadlink
Quick Start:
- Set {{baseUrl}} to https://api.dome9.com
- Use Basic authentication (username/password)
- POST a JSON body containing the searchRequest to receive a download link (or to request the generation of an export and a link).
Parameters Explained:
- searchRequest (object, required): Search request payload for protected assets. Common field:
  - recipients (array[string], optional): recipients for email delivery. (If API supports additional options for link generation they would appear in the body; this page documents recipients.)
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Ensure the body is valid JSON and searchRequest is well-formed.
- 401 Unauthorized: Provide valid Basic credentials.
- 404 Not Found: The requested export/job does not exist (if referencing an existing job id).
Edge Cases:
- The returned download link may be time-limited; download it before it expires.
- Large exports may generate asynchronous jobs and the download link may be returned once generation completes.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Not specified on this page.

data.name: Get Assessment Executive ReportCSV
data.description:
Retrieves a CSV executive report for a specific assessment.
Documentation: Get Assessment Executive ReportCSV
Quick Start:
- Use HTTP GET against the assessment's ExecutiveReport CSV path.
- Authentication: Basic Auth (username/password) is required.
- Minimum required: provide assessmentId (int64) in the path and valid Basic credentials.
Parameters Explained:
- assessmentId (path, required): The numeric identifier (int64) of the assessment to export. Example placeholder: {{assessmentId}}.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid Basic credentials. Ensure {{username}} and {{password}} are correct.
- 404 Not Found: assessmentId not found. Verify the ID is correct and that the assessment exists.
- 400 Bad Request: Malformed request (e.g., invalid assessmentId format). Ensure assessmentId is a valid integer.
- 500 Internal Server Error: Server-side problem; retry after a short delay and contact support if it persists.
Edge Cases:
- The endpoint returns CSV content (binary/text) — some HTTP clients may need to explicitly accept text/csv and handle the raw response body accordingly.
- Large reports may be sizable; streaming or saving to disk is recommended for large CSV responses.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- The documentation page does not list explicit rate limits. Follow typical API best practices (throttle retries, exponential backoff). If your account has specific quotas, consult account billing/limits documentation or support.

data.name: Export Word Count in CSV format
data.description:
Exports the Word Count report in CSV format for the specified parameters.
Documentation: https://api-reference.smartling.com/#operation/exportWordCountReport
Quick Start:
- Authenticate and obtain a Bearer token.
- Provide startDate, endDate, and accountUid query parameters.
- Call the GET /word-count/csv endpoint. The response will be CSV (text/csv).
Parameters Explained:
- startDate (required): Limit words processed on or after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Timezone: America/NewYork.
- endDate (required): Limit words processed on or before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Timezone: America/NewYork.
- accountUid (required): The account's unique identifier.
- projectIds, jobUids, agencyUid, userUids, targetLocaleIds, workflowStepTypes, offset: same semantics as JSON word-count endpoint.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 400 Bad Request: Missing required params or malformed values. Ensure dates and required params are present.
- 401 Unauthorized: Invalid or expired access token.
- 429 Too Many Requests: Throttled — retry after an interval.
- 500 Internal Server Error: Server issue — retry and contact support if persistent.
Edge Cases:
- CSV output may be large for long date ranges; prefer paging/filtered queries or the JSON endpoint with pagination for programmatic processing.
- CSV uses the same America/New_York date interpretation.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Same rate-limiting rules apply; downloading large CSVs may be subject to quotas. Use smaller date ranges if you hit limits.

data.name: Download Export CSV (recent)
data.description:
Downloads the "recent" CSV export file (hash list) for MalwareBazaar.
Documentation: https://bazaar.abuse.ch/export/
Overview:
Retrieves the CSV export file containing recent malware hashes. The Export documentation shows an example curl which downloads the recent CSV export by including your Auth-Key as part of the URI path. Recent datasets include hashes from the last 48 hours and are generated every 5 minutes.
Quick Start:
- Obtain an Auth-Key from the abuse.ch Authentication Portal (https://auth.abuse.ch).
- Replace YOUR-AUTH-KEY-HERE with your Auth-Key in the path segment.
- Issue a GET request to the endpoint; the response is a CSV file (Content-Type: text/csv).
Parameters Explained:
- authKey (required, path) — Your personal Auth-Key issued via the abuse.ch Authentication Portal. Place it in the path segment where shown (/v2/files/exports/{{authKey}}/recent.csv).
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401 Unauthorized / no_api_key: You did not provide a valid Auth-Key. Ensure authKey is correct and not expired. Obtain or renew at https://auth.abuse.ch.
- 403 Forbidden / user_blacklisted: Your API key has been blacklisted. Contact Spamhaus/abuse.ch support.
- 429 Too Many Requests: You are fetching the dataset too frequently. Respect the generation cadence (see Rate Limits).
- 404 Not Found: The path or authKey is invalid. Verify the URL and your authKey.
Edge Cases:
- The export file is generated periodically — a recently generated batch may be empty if no new hashes were added since the last generation.
- The CSV content may include header or comment lines; treat the payload as a CSV file, not JSON.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Recent datasets are generated every 5 minutes; please do not fetch them more often than every 5 minutes.
- Full data dumps are generated once per hour; please do not fetch them more often than once per hour.
Documentation URL: https://bazaar.abuse.ch/export/

Use for: download recent hashes, ingest malware indicators, retrieve CSV exports
